config.title: Warnemünde to Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: How long the cruise day trip really takes, which trains to use, what tickets cost, and when to stay on the coast instead.

items.q: How long does it take to get from Warnemünde to Berlin?
items.a: **A bit over 3 hours door to door each way**: about 5 minutes on foot from the cruise pier to Warnemünde station, 21 minutes on the S-Bahn to Rostock Hauptbahnhof, then roughly 2 hours 40 minutes to Berlin on the direct RE5, or slightly less on the Intercity. Port marketing that says about 2 hours only counts part of the journey.

items.q: Is Berlin worth it as a day trip from a cruise ship in Warnemünde?
items.a: Only when your ship is in port **at least 11 hours**, and comfortably at 12 or more. The round trip costs six and a half hours of travel, so a 9 hour call such as 08:00 to 17:00 leaves barely an hour in the city. With 12 hours in port you get about five focused hours in Berlin's historic centre, which is genuinely enough for a first taste.

items.q: Which train should I take from Warnemünde to Berlin?
items.a: Use one of two patterns: the **RE5 regional train** from Rostock Hauptbahnhof, reached by a short S-Bahn ride, which runs direct to Berlin Hauptbahnhof (for example 06:03 from Warnemünde arriving 09:13), or the **Intercity**, which is faster but stops at Berlin Ostkreuz on the eastern ring instead of Hauptbahnhof. From Ostkreuz, any S-Bahn toward the centre reaches Alexanderplatz in minutes.

items.q: What do train tickets from Warnemünde to Berlin cost?
items.a: **Advance saver fares start around 18 to 25 euros each way** but lock you to one train. The flexible fare costs more and works on any train that day, which is safer for the return leg. For 2 to 5 people on a Saturday or Sunday call, the **Quer-durchs-Land day ticket (51 euros plus 12 per extra person)** covers regional trains all day; on weekdays it only starts at 09:00. The Intercity is a long-distance train and needs its own DB ticket; regional day tickets and the Deutschlandticket are not accepted on it.

items.q: What can I see in Berlin in five hours from a cruise?
items.a: The historic core on one walkable line from Berlin Hauptbahnhof: the **Reichstag** building, the **Brandenburg Gate**, **Unter den Linden**, **Museum Island** with the Berlin Cathedral, and **Alexanderplatz** under the TV Tower, where trains take you back. Skip anything needing a timed ticket, eat a quick bakery or currywurst lunch, and keep the museums for a longer future visit.

items.q: What should I do if Berlin does not fit my port times?
items.a: Stay local, and not as a consolation prize: **Warnemünde** has a wide Baltic beach, a lighthouse and an old fishing harbour five minutes from the pier, and **Rostock**, 21 minutes away by S-Bahn, has a walkable Hanseatic old town around the Marienkirche with its astronomical clock. A calm coastal day beats a rushed Berlin sprint whenever the math is tight.
